uiowa.name: University of Iowa public campus bins
uiowa.description: Public student recycling and landfill stations; NOT Iowa City curbside collection or department/laboratory waste procedures.
uiowa.guidance: Empty, clean and dry containers/paper before recycling. A photo alone cannot confirm food contamination, resin code or battery chemistry.

paper.instructions: Recycle only clean, dry paper without food or grease residue.

cardboard.instructions: Flatten cardboard; recycle only when clean and dry.

carton.instructions: Empty, clean and dry beverage/food cartons are accepted.

plastic_container.instructions: Recycle clean, dry, empty plastic containers; do not interpret this as acceptance of all plastic objects.

metal_can.instructions: Recycle clean, dry, empty metal food and beverage containers.

glass.instructions: Glass is excluded from ordinary campus recycling. Handle broken glass safely; laboratory glass requires separate guidance.

plastic_bag.instructions: Plastic bags are excluded from campus recycling bins. Reuse or use a separate film collection where available.

plastic_film.instructions: Keep soft plastic film and packaging out of campus recycling bins.

plastic_utensil.instructions: Do not place plastic utensils in container-only recycling.

foam.instructions: Styrofoam is not accepted in campus recycling bins.

trash.instructions: Use regular landfill bins for nonhazardous everyday waste; food-contaminated items are not recycling.

glass_bottle.instructions: Glass is excluded from campus recycling bins.

paper_towel.instructions: Not accepted in ordinary recycling; check whether a separate compost program is available.

napkin.instructions: Not accepted in ordinary recycling; check whether a separate compost program is available.

plastic_packet.instructions: Plastic wrappers and packets do not qualify as rigid plastic containers.

foil.instructions: Campus recycling poster specifies metal containers, but does not establish blanket acceptance of foil. Ask facilities for item-specific guidance.

plastic_other.instructions: Resin-code and material appearance alone do not confirm acceptance. Refer to campus item-specific guidance.

glove.instructions: Ordinary and contaminated/hazardous gloves have different handling requirements; confirm use before disposal.

book_hardcover.instructions: Check reuse, donation, or campus collection options before disposal.

battery.instructions: Check battery chemistry: lithium-ion, rechargeable and button batteries require EHS or approved collection; university guidance lists ordinary alkaline batteries as trash. Never assume chemistry from an image.

electronics.instructions: University-owned electronics/e-waste are handled by UI Surplus; personal devices may have separate drop-off options.

light_bulb.instructions: Bulb type matters: fluorescent/mercury lamps use a collection process, while ordinary incandescent lamps may go in trash. Contact General Stores or EHS as appropriate.

aerosol_can.instructions: Do not place pressurized spray cans in ordinary campus bins; contact EHS for the appropriate disposal process.

sharps.instructions: Do not place exposed sharps into standard recycling; seek an approved sharps-collection process.

medication.instructions: Do not decide disposal of medicines solely from a photo; use an appropriate drug take-back or authorized guidance.

plastic.instructions: Cannot determine whether plastic is an accepted empty container, bag, film or utensil from the generic material label.

metal.instructions: Campus recycling is for metal containers; a generic metal label does not prove this object is a container.

rubber.instructions: Rubber objects differ in disposal requirements; tires and specialty rubber require separate guidance.

polystyrene.instructions: Not accepted in campus recycling bins.

textile.instructions: Reuse or donate usable textiles; ordinary textiles are not accepted in standard recycling.

tetrapak.instructions: Empty, clean and dry cartons are accepted.

celluloseacetate.instructions: Retired model category; object-specific disposal must be confirmed.
